overview: This table sets the menu themes players can choose, including each theme's label, music, pictures, movies, and unlock requirements.
description: Defines selectable main-menu themes: their label and BGM IDs, thumbnail texture names, per-screen background movie names, and the save-data progress flags that unlock them.

Id.simple: Which menu theme this is, so the game can remember the player's choice.
Id.technical: FName row key and DataTable import key (exported as ID). PreparePhase reads the uint8 save-header index StudioMainMenuThemeIndex_38E: 0xFF leaves ThemeId NAME_None, otherwise it takes the ID at that position in the table/row-name-ordered row list, using row 0 when the index is out of range. FindThemeRow uses StudioName_17D8 only when the supplied ID is NAME_None; that name is set at startup/debug boot by DTM_PickTitleRowName from the unlocked rows. FindThemeRow scans MainMenuThemeDataTables and returns the row only if GameMainMenuWidget_IsThemeUnlocked passes; a missing or locked ID falls back to the first row of the first non-empty table without rechecking the fallback's flags. OnMainMenuThemeSelected writes the row's position in the collected rows to the save header (0xFF for NAME_None; an unknown non-None ID returns without a write), and the list refresh compares row IDs to skip rebuilding an unchanged list.

Id_Text.simple: The words shown for this theme in the menu list, such as Default or The Shibuya Incident.
Id_Text.technical: FName text ID passed to MainMenuThemeText->SetTextIdOnly when a theme-list item receives focus; GameWidgetTextBlock sends SYS_-prefixed IDs to GameTextManager, which resolves them from SystemTextDataTable. The exported IDs are SYS_MAIN_MENU_THEME_LABEL_0101/0102/0103 (English 'Default', 'Hidden Inventory/Premature Death', 'The Shibuya Incident' in the SystemTextDataTable export). The row-less random entry instead uses SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0042.

Id_Bgm.simple: The music that plays on the main menu while this theme is selected.
Id_Bgm.technical: FName passed to PlayBgm in main-menu phase state 0 and again after a new theme is selected: PlayBgm(Id_Bgm, 0.0f start time, MainMenuTop_BgmFadeTime = 0.5f, bLoop = true). PlayBgm returns early when BGM is disabled or the cue is already current, fades out the previous cue over the same duration and loads the new cue; the fade comes from the phase constant, not from the row. The three exported IDs (BGM_MENU, BGM_BATTLE_DLC_01, BGM_DEMO_10) are also rows in BgmDataTable.

ThumbnailTextureName.simple: The large picture of this theme shown in the theme list on screens with a high resolution.
ThumbnailTextureName.technical: FName selected by ApplyResolution when the width in pixels (current screen-resolution X on list set/rebuild, callback width on resolution changes) is at or above HighResolutionThreshold (3840), then resolved with FindDynamicLoadTexture for the thumbnail brush. Main-menu phase state 0 creates WidgetTexture loaders for this and SmallThumbnailTextureName for every collected theme row (alongside banner textures); state 1 adds the loaded textures to the widget manager's dynamic texture map.

SmallThumbnailTextureName.simple: The smaller picture of this theme shown in the theme list on less sharp screens.
SmallThumbnailTextureName.technical: FName selected by ApplyResolution when the width in pixels is below HighResolutionThreshold (3840); at or above the threshold the large ThumbnailTextureName is used instead. It is also included in the startup WidgetTexture prefetch for every theme row and inserted into the dynamic texture map once loading completes.

VsPlayerMovieFileName.simple: The background movie that plays on the Vs Player screen with this theme. The theme list also plays a short preview of this movie when you highlight the theme.
VsPlayerMovieFileName.technical: FString selected by GetCursorMovieFileName for EGameMainMenuType::VsPlayer; main-menu load step 0 appends '.usm' and passes it to MovieWidget->SetMovieFile. The focused theme-list item also plays this same field with '.usm' appended (after its fade delay, only while the owner list is focused on that entry), regardless of the currently highlighted menu. Like all eight movie strings it defaults to the empty FString in the reconstructed row constructor.

VsEnemyMovieFileName.simple: The background movie that plays on the Vs Enemy screen with this theme.
VsEnemyMovieFileName.technical: FString selected by GetCursorMovieFileName for EGameMainMenuType::VsEnemy; main-menu load step 0 appends '.usm' before MovieWidget->SetMovieFile. An empty string is the row constructor default and prevents SetMovieFile at that step, leaving the load step at 0.

UserProgressFlag.simple: What the player must have unlocked before this theme appears, such as the matching downloaded content. Themes with no requirements are always available.
UserProgressFlag.technical: TArray<int32>. GameMainMenuWidget_IsThemeUnlocked (the same predicate used by DTM_PickTitleRowName) drops -1 entries, treats an empty result as unlocked, and otherwise requires any flag's bit in GameManager::UserInfo.UserProgressFlagWords: word = uint32(Flag) >> 2, bit = uint32(Flag) & 3, with word >= 128 rejected (so other negative values cannot unlock). Exported rows use [-1,-1], [6,-1] and [7,-1]; flags 6 and 7 are the DLC07 and DLC08 entitlement bits set/cleared by GM_DiffDlcEntitlements. The gate controls which rows are added to the theme list, HasSelectableThemes (>=2 unlocked rows, excluding the trailing random entry), and the startup random pool; FindThemeRow's fallback ignores the gate.

notes: The sole export has three themes (MAIN_MENU_THEME_01..03): a default row plus rows gated by progress flags 6 and 7. Their movie base names end in _DLC01/_DLC02; flags 6 and 7 are the DLC07 and DLC08 entitlement bits in GameDlcEntitlementTable. The exported BGM IDs and text IDs also occur in BgmDataTable and SystemTextDataTable.

The manager stores MainMenuThemeDataTables as a TArray and its row/fallback helpers walk every table, but StartInitialLoading registers only one loader keyed MainMenuThemeDataTable (duplicate loader names are discarded); the export contains one asset, so no additional shards or localization/platform variants were observed.

Movie names are stored without '.usm'. The main-menu background loader appends it and does not call SetMovieFile for an empty name, leaving MovieLoadStep at 0; the focused list-item thumbnail preview appends '.usm' without an empty-name check once the movie widget is idle.

The trailing theme-list entry has no row: it uses the widget's RandomImage/SmallRandomImage members (bound outside this table), SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0042 and NAME_None. Selecting it writes 0xFF to the save header; FindThemeRow(NAME_None) then resolves the startup StudioName_17D8 pick rather than drawing a fresh random theme at selection time.

The saved theme index is a uint8 position in the table/row-name-ordered row list (default 0); an out-of-range value selects row 0, and an unknown non-None selection returns before saving. Changing table contents or order can therefore change which theme a saved index means.

The reconstructed row constructor initializes only the eight movie FStrings to TEXT(""); FName fields default to NAME_None and UserProgressFlag to an empty TArray. All exported rows supply explicit values for every field.

Retail UMG widget trees (WBP_MainMenu/WBP_MainMenuTheme) and their bound text/image/movie widgets are Blueprint assets, and no retail Blueprint, asset registry, .usm files or CRI cue sheets were available; widget wiring and media-asset existence are inferred from reconstructed C++ plus exported IDs rather than observed in retail assets.

usages.detail: Registers the MainMenuThemeDataTable loader and resolves its loaded UDataTable into MainMenuThemeDataTables.
Fallback helper returns the first row of the first non-empty table.
Startup/debug-boot picker filters unlocked rows and returns a row ID for GameManager::StudioName_17D8, falling back to the first row when none are unlocked.
FindThemeRow resolves the saved-index/StudioName row and checks its unlock gate; PreparePhase state 0 uses the resulting row for BGM and texture prefetch.
Theme selection writes the row index to the save header, replays the BGM and calls ApplyMainMenuTheme.
Builds list items from unlocked rows, appends one row-less random entry, and skips rebuilding when the row IDs are unchanged.
Shows the focused theme's text ID, or the generic random label for the row-less entry.
Shared unlock predicate interpreting UserProgressFlag against the save's progress words.
HasSelectableThemes requires at least two unlocked rows, not counting the trailing random entry.
Selects the background movie base name for the current CursorMenu from CurrentThemeRow.
Asynchronous movie load steps append '.usm', call SetMovieFile/OpenMovie and report readiness; an empty name leaves step 0.
Chooses the large or small thumbnail FName by width and resolves it through FindDynamicLoadTexture.
Focused list-item preview uses VsPlayerMovieFileName + '.usm' regardless of the highlighted main-menu screen.
